nahhas-irab:1-1.t: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): there are three ways in it: the genitive as a naʿt (adjective); the nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or the accusative as praise. Sībawayh reported «الحمد لله أهلَ الحمد», which is like it. Likewise (جاعِلِ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا); tanwīn is not permissible in it because it refers to the past. (رُسُلًا) is a second object; and it is said: on the implication of a «فاعل», because a «فاعل» (active participle) referring to the past, when it is in a genitive construct, does not govern anything. [Translator's note: «على إضمار فاعل» is as written; the sense appears to be that «رسلاً» is governed by an implied verb, since the participle in the past sense cannot govern.] (أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ) is a naʿt; Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. possessors of wings. (مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) are diptotes because there are two causes in them: one of them is that they are deflected forms (maʿdūla), and this is agreed upon; there is disagreement about the second, because the early grammarians did not mention it. Abū Isḥāq said: the second cause is that it was deflected while indefinite. Others said: the second cause is that it is an adjective. A third view is that it is deflected from «اثنين اثنين» ("two by two"), and that is a second cause.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: The grammarians permitted outside the Qurʾān: «فلا ممسك له» (then there is none to withhold it — masculine), according to the wording of «ما», while «لها» (feminine) is according to the meaning. They permitted: (وَما يُمْسِكْ) «فلا مرسل لها», according to the meaning of «ما». And they permitted «فلا ممسكٌ لها» [in the nominative], in the sense of «ليس», and likewise «فلا مرسلٌ له». And they permitted «ما يفتحُ الله للناس من رحمة», with «ما» in the sense of «الذي» (that which).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ (3)

(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ): this is the reading of Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Shaqīq ibn Salama, Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «هل من خالق غيرِ الله». [Translator's note: the source prints this second reading without vowels; the genitive «غيرِ» is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, as the following "the genitive according to the wording" indicates.] It is permissible to put «غير» in the accusative as an exception. The nominative is from two angles: one of them in the sense of "Is there any creator except Allah?", meaning "There is no creator except Allah"; the second way is that it is a naʿt (adjective) on the position, because the meaning is "Is there a creator other than Allah?". The genitive is according to the wording. Ḥammād ibn Salama said: Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl told us: I said to al-Ḥasan: "Who created evil?" He said: "Glory be to Allah! Is there any creator other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Allah created good and evil."

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): as a consolation for him ﷺ. (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ): Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. the return of matters is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He will recompense whoever gave the lie and give victory to those of His messengers who were given the lie.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ فَلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا): Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: the delusion of the life of this world is that a person is distracted by its pleasures and its trials from working for the Hereafter, until (يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي) [al-Fajr: 24]. (وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ): Shuʿba reported from Simāk (وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ) with ḍamma on the ghayn [«الغُرور»]. There are three views on it. Among them: that it is the plural of «غارّ» (deceiver), as you say «جالس» and «جلوس»; this is the best of what has been said about it, and its meaning is then like the meaning of «الغَرور» (the Deceiver). [Translator's note: the source reads «مع غار», evidently for «جمع غارّ» "plural of غارّ".] Abū Ḥātim said: «الغُرور» is the plural of «غَرّ», and «غَرّ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). The third view is that «الغُرور» is a maṣdar; this is far-fetched according to Abū Isḥāq, because «غررته» is transitive, and the maṣdar of a transitive verb is only on the pattern «فَعْل», as in «ضربته ضرباً», except for a few things that were heard and on which no analogy is built: they said «لزمته لزوماً» and «نهكه المرض نهوكاً». [Translator's note: the source prints «لزما», but the example requires the anomalous «لزوماً».] As for the meaning of this word, the best of what has been said about it is what Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: delusion concerning Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is that a person commits sins and then hopes for forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ): «عدوّ» may be in the sense of «معادٍ» (one who shows enmity), and then it takes the dual, the plural and the feminine; or it may be in the sense of attribution, and then it is singular in every case, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77]; and on this basis the feminine is also «عدوّ». As for the statement of some grammarians that the wāw is weak, so they brought the hāʾ [i.e. «عدوّة»], it is an error; rather, the wāw is a strong letter. (فَاتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّا): two objects. (إِنَّما يَدْعُوا حِزْبَهُ): «ما» has restrained «إنّ» from governing, so the verb came after it. (لِيَكُونُوا مِنْ أَصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) may be a badal (substitute) for «أصحاب», and then it is in the position of the genitive; it may be a badal for «حزبه», and then it is in the position of the accusative; or it may be a badal for the wāw [in «ليكونوا»], and then it is in the position of the nominative. A fourth view, and it is the best of them: it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ). As for (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا), it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is (لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (أَفَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ): «مَن» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted because of what indicates it. Al-Kisāʾī said: and what indicates it is (فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَراتٍ), the meaning being: "Is the one to whom the evil of his deed has been made fair-seeming, so that he sees it as good — [for such] has your soul gone out in sorrows over them?" He said: this is good, elegant Arabic speech which few know. What al-Kisāʾī said is the best of what has been said about the verse, because of the indication of the omitted part which he mentioned. [Translator's note: the source reads «لما ذكره فمن الدلالة», evidently for «لما ذكره من الدلالة».] The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade the Prophet ﷺ from intense distress over them and grief for them, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 3]; the people of tafsīr said: i.e. killing yourself. It was read to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, who said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī told us: I asked al-Aṣmaʿī about the saying of the Prophet ﷺ concerning the people of Yemen, "They are the softest of hearts and the most «أبخع» in obedience" — what does "أبخع طاعة" mean? He said: the most sincere in obedience. I said to him: "The people of tafsīr, Mujāhid and others, say about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ) that its meaning is 'killing yourself'." He said: "It is from exactly that; it is as though, from the intensity of his sincerity towards them, he were killing himself." The reading of Abū Jaʿfar is «فلا تُذْهِبْ نفسَك» [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the same vowelling as the standard one, (فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ); the transitive form given here is the known reading of Abū Jaʿfar], and the two meanings are close. «حسرات» is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ): the implied form according to al-Farrāʾ is "whoever desires knowledge of might". Likewise others among the people of knowledge said: whoever desires knowledge of the might with which there is no abasement — because when might leads to abasement, it is itself exposed to abasement, and the might with which there is no abasement belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (جَمِيعاً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq rendered its meaning: whoever desires, by worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to be mighty through it — Allah will make him mighty in the Hereafter and in this world. (إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ): the statement is complete. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «إليه يصعد الكلامُ». «الكلم» is the plural of «كلمة». The people of tafsīr — Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, Shahr ibn Ḥawshab and others — said: the meaning is that righteous action raises the good word. This is a refutation of the Murjiʾa. (وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ) is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or on the implication of a verb. As for its being nominative in the sense of "and righteous action raises it", that is an error, because when the agent precedes the verb it is not made nominative by the verb. This is the view of all the grammarians, except something that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, that he permitted «زيد قام» in the sense of «قام زيد». Abū Jaʿfar said: what shows you the unsoundness of this is the Arabs' saying «الزيدان قاما»; were it as he said, it would be said «الزيدان قام». (وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ) in the sense of "those who do evil deeds", so «السيئات» is an object; and it is possible that the implied form is "those who do evil", so «السيئات» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين». (وَمَكْرُ أُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ, and «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ, and (يَبُورُ) is the khabar of the second; it may also be a khabar of the first, with «هو» redundant (zāʾida). [Translator's note: the source reads «هذا زائدة», evidently for «هو زائدة».] One says «بار يبور» when something perishes; from it is «بارت السوق» (the market became stagnant), and "we seek refuge in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from the stagnation (bawār) of the unmarried woman".

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: meaning Ādam ﷺ, and the implied form on this basis is "He created your origin from dust". (ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ): he said: i.e. that which He brought forth from the loins of your fathers. (ثُمَّ جَعَلَكُمْ أَزْواجاً): he said: i.e. He paired some of you with others. (وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ وَلا يُنْقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ): ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn told us from al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥamd, who said: Ibn ʿAwāna told us from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "No one is granted long life except that his lifespan is written: how many years is it? how many months? how many days? and how many hours? Then it is written at his lifespan: so much has decreased, so much has decreased, until the decrease matches the lifespan." The position of al-Farrāʾ on the meaning of (وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ) is: none has his life lengthened, and none has [his] life shortened — meaning another — i.e. nor is the other's life decreased from the life of that one, (إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ). (إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ): its verb is «يسر»; and were you to name a person with it, it would be fully declined, because it is on the pattern «فعيل».

nahhas-irab:12-13.t:
(وَما يَسْتَوِي الْبَحْرانِ هذا عَذْبٌ فُراتٌ): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: «فرات» is sweet, and «أجاج» is salty and bitter. Ṭalḥa read «وهذا مَلِحٌ أجاج» with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām, without alif. As for «المالح», it is one who puts salt in something to improve it. (وَمِنْ كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا): there is no disagreement that this is from both of them together. (وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَها): the position of Abū Isḥāq is that the ornaments are only extracted from the salt [water], and it was said "from both" because they are mixed. Others said: the shells, about which it says "ornaments", of pearls and others, are only extracted from places where there is both sweet and salt, such as springs. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd held a third view, which is the best of them; he said: the ornaments are extracted from the salt [water] specifically, and in his view this is not because they are mixed; rather, the two were joined together and then a statement was made about one of them, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (وَمِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) [Yūnus: 67] [Translator's note: this wording is in al-Qaṣaṣ: 73; Yūnus: 67 has a different wording], and as you say: "Had you seen al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥajjāj, you would have seen good and evil," and as you say: "Had you seen al-Aṣmaʿī and Sībawayh, you would have filled your hand with lexicon and grammar"; the meaning of this is known, and it is frequent, eloquent speech. So it is here: (وَمِنْ كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَها) — they are together in the first, and the salt is alone in the second, so they become together in all of this. He said: (وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَواخِرَ), i.e. in the salt [water] specifically; were it not so, He would have said «فيهما» (in both). «مخرت السفينة تمخَر وتمخُر» is said when the ship cleaves the water, as Ṭarafa said: [al-Ṭawīl] 354-
يشقّ حباب الماء حيزومها بها ... كما قسم التّرب المفايل باليد
(Its breast cleaves the bubbles of the water with it, as the player of al-fiyāl divides the earth with his hand.)
And it was said: the appointed term here is the Resurrection, because with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is appointed for a known time. (وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ ما يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْ قِطْمِيرٍ): ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: «القطمير» is the skin of the date-stone.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: (إِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ لا يَسْمَعُوا دُعاءَكُمْ): a condition and its apodosis. (وَلَوْ سَمِعُوا مَا اسْتَجابُوا لَكُمْ): it has the meaning of the first, even though «لو» is not used to give a conditional apodosis [in the jussive]. [Translator's note: the source reads «وإن كانت لولا يجازى بها», evidently «وإن كانت لو لا يجازى بها».] Qatāda said: (مَا اسْتَجابُوا لَكُمْ) — they would not follow you nor accept from you. (وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِكُمْ): Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. they will say, "It was not us they worshipped." (وَلا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ): Qatāda said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that this will happen from you on the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ): lightening the second hamza is the best of the ways according to al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him; it is also permissible to lighten the first, to drop it, to lighten both together, and to pronounce both fully. (وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): «هو» may be redundant (zāʾida), having no position in iʿrāb, or it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), so that its position is nominative.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: (إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ): a condition and its apodosis, and there is an omission in it which the Arabs use frequently; the implied form is "If He wills to remove you, He will remove you". From «يشأ» the ḍamma that was on the hamza was dropped, and when it became quiescent, the alif before it was dropped. (وَيَأْتِ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «يذهبكم».

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
(بَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ): «مَيْت» and «مَيِّت» are one [in meaning], and likewise «مَيْتة» and «مَيِّتة» are one. This is the view of the skilled grammarians. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is the view of the Basrans, and he made no exception of anyone, and he adduced decisive proofs for it from the speech of the Arabs. He recited: [al-Khafīf] 352-
ليس من مات فاستراح بميت ... إنّما الميت ميّت الأحياء
إنّما الميت من يعيش كئيبا ... كاسفا باله قليل الرّخاء
(Not he who died and found rest is dead; the dead is only the dead among the living. The dead is only he who lives in gloom, downcast in mind, with little ease.)
It is also transmitted as «قليل الرّجاء» (with little hope). He said: do you see any difference between «مَيْت» and «مَيِّت»? And he recited: [al-Basīṭ] 353-
هينون لينون أيسار بنو يسر ... سوّاس مكرمة أبناء أيسار
(Gentle, mild, generous players at the lots, sons of generosity, managers of noble deeds, sons of generous men.)
He said: they have agreed that his saying «هَيْنون» and «هَيِّنون» are one, and likewise «مَيْت» and «مَيِّت», and «سَيْد» and «سَيِّد». He said: Sībawayh claimed that their «كان كينونة» and «صار صيرورة» are originally «كيّنونة» and «صيّرورة», and likewise «قيدودة». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd refuted the Kufans' statement that it is on the pattern «فَعْلول» from two angles: one, that there is no «فَعْلول» in the speech of the Arabs; and the second, that had it been as they said, it would have been with wāw. [Translator's note: the doubled forms «كيّنونة», «صيّرونة» are implied by the argument; the source writes both forms identically without shadda.] Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear, good argument regarding «كينونة», because it is from «الكون», and regarding «القيدودة», because it is from «الأقود». (كَذلِكَ النُّشُورُ), i.e. thus will you be brought to life after you have died; from «نشر الإنسان نشوراً» when he comes to life, and «أنشره الله» (Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revived him).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (وَلا تَزِرُ) is cut off from what precedes it. The original is «تَوْزِر»; the wāw was dropped in conformity with «يَزِر». (وازِرَةٌ) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun, i.e. "a burdened soul"; and likewise (وَإِنْ تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ): al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. a heavily laden soul or beast; he said: this applies to the masculine and the feminine. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "and if a heavily laden one calls a person (إِلى حِمْلِها)". «الحِمْل» is what is on the back; «حَمْل» of a woman and «حَمْل» of a palm-tree al-Kisāʾī reported with fatḥa only, while Ibn al-Sikkīt reported that «حمل» of a palm-tree takes fatḥa and kasra. (وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى): the implied form according to al-Akhfash's view is "even if the person called were a near relative". Al-Farrāʾ permitted «ولو كان ذو قربى». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is permissible according to Sībawayh, and like it is (وَإِنْ كانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ) [al-Baqara: 280]; «كان» is then in the sense of "occurred", or the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "if among those from whom you demand there is one in difficulty". Sībawayh reported: «الناس مجزيّون بأعمالهم إن خيرٌ فخيرٌ» ("people are recompensed for their deeds: if good, then good") on this [pattern], and «إن خيراً فخيراً» on the first. Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān reported from ʿIkrima that he said: "It has reached me that the Jew and the Christian will see the Muslim man on the Day of Resurrection and say to him: 'Did I not do you a favour? Did I not treat you well?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'Then benefit me.' And the Muslim will keep decreasing his punishment. And a man will come to his father on the Day of Resurrection and say: 'Was I not dutiful to you, compassionate towards you and good to you? You see the state I am in; so give me one of your good deeds, or bear one evil deed for me.' He will say: 'What you have asked of me is small, but I fear what you fear.' And the father will say the like of that to his son, and he will answer him with something similar. And a man will say to his wife: 'Was I not of good companionship to you? Then bear a sin for me; perhaps I will be saved.' She will say: 'That is small, but I fear what you fear.'" Then ʿIkrima recited: (وَإِنْ تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلى حِمْلِها لا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى). (إِنَّما تُنْذِرُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ): he warns all creatures, but He singled out those who fear their Lord because they are the ones who benefit from the warning.

nahhas-irab:19-21.t:
﴿وَما يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ﴾ (19) ﴿وَلا الظُّلُماتُ وَلا النُّورُ﴾ (20) ﴿وَلا الظِّلُّ وَلا الْحَرُورُ﴾ (21)

(وَما يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: the believer and the disbeliever. He said: (الظُّلُماتُ) is misguidance, (النُّورُ) is guidance, (الظِّلُّ) is Paradise, and (الْحَرُورُ) is the Fire. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is "nor the darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the hot wind". It was said: «الحرور» is only by night, and «السموم» is by day; and it was said: «الحرور» is in both. This is the sounder of the two views, because «حرور» is «فعول» from «الحرّ» (heat), and there is in it the meaning of intensity, i.e. harmful heat.
Al-Ḥasan read «وما أنت بمسمعِ من في القبور», the tanwīn being dropped for lightness; i.e. they are like the people of the graves in that they do not benefit from what they hear nor accept it. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard vowelling (وَما أَنْتَ بِمُسْمِعٍ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ); the comment shows that al-Ḥasan's reading is without tanwīn, in genitive construct. The source also has «أهل القبول», evidently for «أهل القبور» "the people of the graves".]

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَبِالزُّبُرِ): and in another place (الزُّبُرِ) [Āl ʿImrān: 184] without bāʾ, and the meaning is the same, except that what is frequent in the speech of the Arabs is without bāʾ, and with what follows also with bāʾ; so the bāʾ, when it enters, is tawkīd (emphasis), or it is the conjoining of a clause to a clause with the verb omitted because the first indicates it.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: You put (مُخْتَلِفاً) in the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «ثمرات», and (أَلْوانُها) is nominative by «مختلف»; it is fit to be a naʿt of «ثمرات» because of the pronoun referring back to it. Its nominative is permissible outside the Qurʾān. Like it: «رأيت رجلاً خارجاً أبوه» ("I saw a man whose father was going out"). (وَمِنَ الْجِبالِ جُدَدٌ): plural of «جُدّة» (streak). Al-Akhfash said: had it been the plural of «جديد», it would have been said «جُدُد», like «رغيف» and «رُغُف». (بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُها): «مختلف» is nominative here and accusative there, because what precedes it here is nominative, so it is a naʿt of it; and it may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: It is said here (أَلْوانُهُ) and there «أَلْوانُها», because its implied form is "and a creation differing in its colours"; and «مختلف» is a naʿt (adjective) put in the place of the qualified noun. The kāf [of «كذلك»] is in the position of a naʿt, because it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). (إِنَّما يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبادِهِ الْعُلَماءُ): Mujāhid said: the learned one is only he who fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: "Fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, suffices as knowledge, and being deluded about Him suffices as ignorance."

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ كِتابَ اللَّهِ وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً يَرْجُونَ تِجارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ﴾ (29)

(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ كِتابَ اللَّهِ): Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» is (يَرْجُونَ تِجارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ).

nahhas-irab:32-33.t: (ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا): this verse is difficult, because He, Mighty and Majestic, said (اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا) and then He, Mighty and Majestic, said (فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ). We had mentioned it before, but we will explain it here with the utmost clarity. A number of the Companions, the Followers and those after them have spoken about it. Among the soundest of what has been reported on that is what was read to Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Imām, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told us from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: «فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ» — he said: the disbeliever. And it was read to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥabīb, from al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā, from Ḥusayn, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: (ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سابِقٌ بِالْخَيْراتِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) — he said: two groups were saved. This is one view; and the implied form in Arabic is then «فمنهم», i.e. "of Our servants", «ظالم لنفسه», i.e. a disbeliever. Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. a sinner (fāsiq). And the pronoun in «يدخلونها» then refers back to the moderate one and the foremost one, not to the wrongdoer. As for the meaning of «الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا», there are two views on it: one is that those chosen are the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, i.e. they were chosen for the message; and it was said: the meaning is those chosen for the Book to be sent down to them, and this is general. And it was said: the pronoun in (يَدْخُلُونَها) refers back to all three classes, on the basis that the wrongdoer here is neither a disbeliever nor a sinner. Among those from whom this view is reported — I mean that those who enter it are these three classes — are ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUqba ibn ʿAmr and ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them. Were it not for our dislike of length, we would have mentioned that with its chains of transmission, though they are not like the first chains in soundness. This view is also soundly transmitted from ʿUbayd ibn ʿAmr, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and others among the Followers. The interpretation according to this view is that the one who wrongs himself is the one who committed minor sins; and the moderate one — Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: he is the one who gives this world its due and the Hereafter its due. So «جنّات عدن يدخلونها» refers back to all of them, according to this explanation and clarification. There is a third view on the verse: «الظالم» is the one who commits major sins, and the moderate one is he who has not merited Paradise by his good deeds exceeding his evil deeds; so «جنّات عدن يدخلونها» refers to those who are foremost in good deeds and no others. [Translator's note: the source reads «الذين سبقونا بالخيرات», evidently for «الذين سبقوا بالخيرات».] This is the view of a group of the people of reasoning; they said: because the pronoun, in strict reasoning, more fittingly belongs to what is next to it. We have mentioned the view of the earlier scholars before this. (يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ): plural of «أسورة», and «أسورة» is the plural of «سِوار» and «سُوار». It has been reported that one says «إسوار», and the plural of «إسوار» is «أساوير»; it has been reported that in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy is «أساوير». Dropping the yāʾ from [the pattern] «مفاعيل» in this is permissible; but what is known is that «الأسوار» is the man who is a good archer among the Persians. (وَلُؤْلُؤاً) [in the accusative] is the reading of the people of Medina. Abū Isḥāq said: because the meaning of «من أساور» and the meaning of «أساور» are one. The genitive is the reading of the people of Kufa, and it is clearer in Arabic, because it is a genitive conjoined to a genitive. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «جنّاتِ عدن يدخلونها» with kasra on the tāʾ, which is then in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for «الخيرات»; and it may be in the position of the accusative according to the dialect of those who say «زيداً ضربته». [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard vowelling (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها).] Some of the people of reasoning claimed that His words, Mighty and Majestic, (يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ) are about the women, because His words, Mighty and Majestic, (مِنْ عِبادِنا) include males and females. This is a clear error, because had it been about the women it would have been «يُحَلَّيْن»; rather it is about the men only — though women may be adorned with it, and when women are adorned with it, it is for their husbands.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ): from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: the Fire. Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: they used to work in this world and toil, and grief would afflict them. Shamir ibn ʿAṭiyya said about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ): he said: the worry over food. He said: (إِنَّ رَبَّنا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ): He forgave them the sins they committed, and appreciated for them the good to which He guided them and which they did.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: (الَّذِي أَحَلَّنا دارَ الْمُقامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): «الذي» may be in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of the noun of «إنّ»; it may be in the position of the nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a khabar (predicate) after the khabar of «إنّ», or as a badal (substitute) for «غفور», or as a badal for the latent pronoun in «شكور»; and it may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: (الْمُقامَةِ) [with ḍamma] is residence, and «المَقامة» [with fatḥa] is the assembly in which one stands. [Translator's note: the source reads «الإمامة», evidently for «الإقامة» "residence".] (لا يَمَسُّنا فِيها نَصَبٌ), i.e. fatigue. «النُّصْب» is evil, and «النُّصُب» is what is set up for slaughter or otherwise. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «ولا يمسّنا فيها لَغوب» with fatḥa on the lām [the source prints (وَلا يَمَسُّنا فِيها لُغُوبٌ)]; it is then a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «الوَقود» and «الطَّهور»; and it was said: it is that from which one becomes weary.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (لَهُمْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ); the khabar may also be (لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا). The nūn was dropped because it is the answer to a negation. Al-Ḥasan read «لا يقضى عليهم فيموتون» by conjunction. Al-Kisāʾī said: (وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ) [al-Mursalāt: 36] is with nūn in the muṣḥaf because it is the end of a verse, and (لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا) is without nūn because it is not the end of a verse; and in each of them what is permissible in the other is permissible.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: (وَهُمْ يَصْطَرِخُونَ فِيها): the ṭāʾ is substituted for a tāʾ, because ṭāʾ is more like ṣād, both being velarized (muṭbaq) letters. One says «اصطرخ» when one cries for help. (رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا), i.e. they say. (نَعْمَلْ صالِحاً) is the answer to the request, i.e. if You bring us out we will do righteousness other than what we used to do. (أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ), i.e. then it will be said to them. Abū Hurayra reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever is given life to sixty years, Allah has left him no excuse in [length of] life." Likewise Sahl ibn Saʿd reported from the Prophet ﷺ something of similar meaning. Ibn ʿAbbās said about His words, Mighty and Majestic, (أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ ما يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَنْ تَذَكَّرَ): he said: sixty years. (وَجاءَكُمُ النَّذِيرُ), i.e. the warner; and in [the pattern] «فعيل» there is the meaning of intensity. It was said: by it is meant the Prophet ﷺ; and it was said: it is whoever warned them; and it was said: by it is meant grey hair; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: When it is without tanwīn, it is fit for the past, the future and the present; and when it has tanwīn, it may not be for the past.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلائِفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): plural of «خليفة», i.e. you succeed those who were before you. In this there is the meaning of warning and taking heed, i.e. so beware lest punishment descend on you as it descended on those before you. (فَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ) is like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82], i.e. the punishment of his disbelief. (وَلا يَزِيدُ الْكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا مَقْتاً): two objects; and likewise (وَلا يَزِيدُ الْكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ إِلَّا خَساراً).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ شُرَكاءَكُمُ) is accusative by [the verb of] seeing, and its nominative is not permissible. The nominative may be permissible according to Sībawayh in their saying «قد علمتُ زيدٌ أبو من هو» ("I know Zayd — whose father he is"), because Zayd is, in meaning, the one asked about; but if you said «أرأيتَ زيداً أبو من هو؟», the nominative would not be permissible. The difference between them is that the meaning of this is "inform me about him"; and likewise the meaning of this [verse] is: inform me about your partners whom you call upon besides Allah — did you worship them because they have a share in the creation of the heavens, or did they create anything of the earth, or did We give them a Book with this? I.e. or do they have a Book which We sent down to them with partnership, or [stating] that We commanded them to worship them? So in this is a refutation of everyone who worships other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because they do not find in any of the Books that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that other than Him be worshipped.
«على بيّنات منه» is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī; Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْهُ). Abū Jaʿfar said: the two meanings are close, except that the reading «بيّنات» is preferable, because whoever read «على بيّنة» must either have differed from the main body of the text [of the muṣḥaf], or have brought it according to the dialect of those who say «جاءني طلحة», pausing with tāʾ [i.e. «طلحت» rather than «طلحه»]; and this is an anomalous, rare dialect.
(بَلْ إِنْ يَعِدُ الظَّالِمُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً): «إن» is in the sense of «ما» (not), and that is why you made the verb nominative. (بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً): «بعضهم» [is a badal (substitute) for «الظالمون»]. [Translator's note: the source breaks off after «بعضهم»; the bracketed completion is added.] (إِلَّا غُرُوراً), i.e. except delusion with falsehood.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولا): «أن» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of "disliking [that]", or it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "Allah prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing". (وَلَئِنْ زالَتا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُما مِنْ أَحَدٍ): al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "and were they to cease, none would hold them after Him", and «إن» is in the sense of «ما». [Translator's note: the source prints «أان», a misprint for «إن».] He said: it is like His words, the Exalted: (وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ) [al-Rūm: 51].

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): Abū Isḥāq said: they had sworn and exerted themselves [in swearing]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the oath falls on (لَيَكُونُنَّ أَهْدى مِنْ إِحْدَى الْأُمَمِ). Al-Akhfash said: «إحدى» was made feminine because «أمّة» is feminine. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ ما زادَهُمْ إِلَّا نُفُوراً), i.e. from the truth.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
(اسْتِكْباراً) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. out of arrogance towards the truth. (وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it. Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: i.e. and the plotting of polytheism. Abū Jaʿfar said: the root meaning of evil plotting in the language is lying and deception with falsehood. Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «ومكرَ السّيّئْ ولا يحيق المكر السيّئُ إلا بأهله», dropping the case ending from the first and keeping it in the second. [Translator's note: the source prints the reading without vowels and with «ولا يحق» for «ولا يحيق»; the sukūn on the first «السيّئ» is supplied from the explanation.] Abū Isḥāq said: it is a solecism (laḥn) which is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: it became a solecism only because the case ending was dropped from it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd claimed that this is permissible neither in prose nor in poetry, because the case vowels may not be dropped, since they were introduced to distinguish between meanings. Some grammarians considered it too grave that al-Aʿmash, with his eminence and standing, should read this way, and said: he only paused on it, and whoever claimed this from him erred. He said: the proof of this is that it is the end of the statement, and that since the second was not the end of the statement, he gave it its case ending; and the vowel in the second is heavier than in the first, because it is a ḍamma between two kasras. Some grammarians argued for Ḥamza in this with the view of Sībawayh, and that he and others recited: [al-Rajaz] 355-
إذا اعوججن قلت صاحب قوّم ... بالدوّ أمثال السّفين العوّم
(When they swerved, I said: "Companion, straighten [them]" — in the desert, like floating ships.)
And another said: [al-Sarīʿ] 356-
فاليوم أشرب غير مستحقب ... إثما من الله ولا واغل
(So today I drink, not incurring sin before Allah, nor intruding uninvited.)
There is no proof in this, because Sībawayh did not permit it; some grammarians merely reported it. And a report, when it is said to be from some scholar, is no proof — how much less when he only brought it as anomalous and as poetic licence, and he has been contradicted in it. Abū Isḥāq claimed that Abū al-ʿAbbās recited it to him: [al-Rajaz] 357-
إذا اعوججن قلت صاح قوّم
(When they swerved, I said: "O companion, straighten [them].")
and that he recited it «فاليوم فاشرب» with fāʾ. (فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ), i.e. they await only the punishment which descended on the earlier disbelievers. (فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا), i.e. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the punishment befall the disbelievers and made that a practice (sunna) concerning them; so He punishes with the like of it whoever deserves it, and no one is able to change that or divert it.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: Abū Isḥāq said: (لِيُعْجِزَهُ) — to escape Him …

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
(وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِما كَسَبُوا) is with hamza, because the Arabs say «أخذتُ فلاناً بكذا وكذا» ("I took so-and-so to account for such-and-such"), and one does not say «وأخذت». But if you lighten the hamza in «يؤاخذ», it is permissible, and you say «يُواخِذ», changing it into a wāw. If someone says: "Why not change it into an alif, when it has fatḥa?", I say: this is impossible, because what precedes alif is never anything but fatḥa. (عَلى ظَهْرِها) refers back to the earth, which has been mentioned before.
(فَإِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ بَصِيراً): it is not permissible that the governing word of «إذا» be «بصيراً», just as «اليوم أنّ زيداً خارج» is not permissible; rather, what governs it is «جاء», because it resembles the conditional particles, and it is sometimes used as a conditional, as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 358-
إذا قصرت أسيافنا كان وصلها ... خطانا إلى أعدائنا فنضارب
(When our swords fall short, their extension is our steps towards our enemies, and so we strike.)
